sources.summary: Measured relaxation over20ns–200ms and AC susceptibility100Hz–1MHz, using multiple instrument windows. Particle structures showed differing viscosity dependence, challenging a universal inverse-sum relaxation explanation.
sources.support: Instrument cancellation, window stitching and weak-field assumption are explicit; observed response can depend on structure and viscosity.
sources.limitations: Finite excitation transition/sensitivity miss fast and long-tail components; microscopic two-step interpretation is not a unique inverse solution. No biological efficacy inference. The text in section3.3 calls loss-peak frequency proportional to viscosity, which conflicts with the simple tauB proportional to viscosity inverse-frequency prediction; figure direction not independently checked here. Do not use that wording as validation of fpeak proportional to eta.
